root.claim: One deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes outputs $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ on every input $x\#y$ with $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, in worst-case time $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, which refutes an eventual $\Omega(n\lg n)$ lower bound for multiplication in this model.
root.method: Reduce the product to a convolution of radix-$2^b$ digits, carry that convolution through exact changes of problem (Chinese-remainder axes, Gaussian resampling with chirps, a phase twist into $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$) that end in synthetic transforms, make the address movement and butterfly layers of those transforms cheaper with two recursive tape procedures built on fixed linear networks with a rank deficit, then recover the integer product exactly and sum all costs divided by the volume $Tp$.

motivation.text: A transform-based multiplier scans $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ levels, so going below $n\log n$ requires both the data movement and the butterfly arithmetic of a level to cost less than a full scan; the two network-based tape procedures supply exactly those two savings.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The improvement is only the factor $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ with the tiny exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$, yet it is a strict power saving in the logarithm that holds through all input lengths, so $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)\to0$ rather than merely having limit inferior zero.

adds.name: input length
adds.meaning: The number of bits of each of the two operands.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $2^{-182}$ by which the running time beats $n\lg n$ in the power of the logarithm.

adds.name: running time
adds.meaning: The worst-case number of steps of the machine $A$ on inputs with $n$-bit operands.

children.claim: In the fixed-tape model the optimality conjecture asserts, for every fixed machine $A$, constants $c_A>0$ and $N_A$ with $T_A(n)\ge c_An\lg n$ for all $n\ge N_A$; refuting it needs only one machine with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$, and a bound $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ gives the stronger conclusion that this ratio tends to zero through all input lengths.

quote.quote: Its negation requires one machine satisfying $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$.

children.claim: On a fixed number of tapes, two equal $u$-bit address chunks of an array of stored bit volume $V$ can be interchanged in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time, and the normalized butterfly $H_0$ on one selected bit of each of $D\le d$ equal-width address chunks can be applied to arrays of polynomial records in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time, with fixed $\tau<1$ and $\lambda'<1$ (in the algorithm $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ and $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$).
children.method: Supply linear-time stream primitives, build two fixed linear networks whose frame changes need fewer than $Wm$ smaller calls, and turn each network into a recursion on $W$ row streams of volume $V/W$ whose normalized cost grows by the factor $s/W<m^\tau$ per level.

motivation.text: After dividing cost by volume, each procedure becomes a recurrence in which multiplying the chunk or axis count by $m$ multiplies the recursive cost only by $s/W<m$; that strict gap is what produces an exponent below one.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

adds.name: stored bit volume
adds.meaning: The number of data bits stored in the array a procedure acts on, excluding work tapes.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of address bits in each of the two chunks being interchanged.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-50}$ in the interchange bound $O(Vu^\tau)$, chosen with $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$.

adds.name: layer growth exponent
adds.meaning: A fixed upper bound $1-2^{-50}$ for $\log_m(s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c})$, the growth exponent of the butterfly-layer recursion.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-54}$ in the butterfly-layer bound $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $m=h^3=10^6$ of the label space, also the factor by which one recursion level divides the chunk or axis count.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires of the fixed network in use, $W_{\rm b}$ for the bit network or $W_{\rm c}$ for the complex one.

adds.name: smaller-call count
adds.meaning: The number of smaller calls made by one network invocation: the sum over edges of the edge-matrix ranks or residual dimensions.

adds.name: bit wire count
adds.meaning: The number $177176569091445000000$ of wires of the bit network.

adds.name: complex wire count
adds.meaning: The number $1873807244643542670000$ of wires of the complex network.

adds.name: bit rank sum
adds.meaning: The sum $W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$ of the rational ranks of all edge matrices of the bit network.

adds.name: complex kernel count
adds.meaning: The number $W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$ of directional kernels over all edges of the complex network.

children.claim: For a fixed radix $q\ge2$, an array of volume $V$ stored in lexicographic address order (addresses implicit in positions, not stored) admits in $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of tapes: any fixed permutation of the digits at two radix-$q$ positions, a move of one digit, a split on one digit followed by a fixed pointwise map and a merge, and the cyclic distribution of whole rows of $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$ into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$ (with the inverse merge when $W$ divides $R$), counters, resets and head returns included.

quote.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes:

children.claim: If a target field $y\in[Q]$, $Q=q^b$ with $q$ prime, follows its control fields, the update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\pmod Q$ costs $O(V)$ whenever the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time (each fiber of $Q$ blocks is split at $Q-a$ and its two pieces merged in the opposite order, and $b^{O(1)}=O(Q)$ is absorbed), and multiplying $y$ by a fixed rational unit prime to $q$, or by its inverse, also costs $O(V)$.

quote.quote: costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the fixed number of control values.

children.claim: Each of the two fixed networks, the bit network with $W_{\rm b}$ wires and the complex network with $W_{\rm c}$ wires, exchanges two banks of $N$ values with a sign while restoring every scratch wire, and carries frames whose edge changes need in total $s<Wm$ smaller operations: $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$ and $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$, so that $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$ and each recursive level costs a factor $s/W<m$.
children.method: Build a three-stage scalar exchange from three-element subsets of $[h]$, attach nested nondegenerate subspaces of $F^{\otimes3}$ as labels so that an edge's frame change costs the dimension of its orthogonal residual, and count: the signed changes telescope to $Wm-2N$ and only central wires lose dimension, a total $L<N/2$.

motivation.text: Signed label changes cancel at every gate and so sum to sink minus source dimensions, $Wm-2N$; the absolute total exceeds this only by twice the dimension lost on decreasing edges, so keeping that loss below $N/2$ pushes the number of smaller operations strictly below $Wm$.

quote.quote: The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

children.salient: Every one of the $W$ roles, scratch roles included, ends up transformed by the full $m$-dimensional endpoint operator, yet the edges together need strictly fewer than $Wm$ unit operations: the exchange of the $N$ data roles leaves a deficit of $N-2L_{\rm b}$ (bit) or $2N-2L_{\rm c}$ (complex), tiny relative to $Wm$ but fixed and positive.

adds.name: ground-set size
adds.meaning: The number $h=100$ of points whose three-element subsets index the banks.

adds.name: triple count
adds.meaning: The number $v=\binom{100}3=161700$ of three-element subsets of $[h]$.

adds.name: bank size
adds.meaning: The number $N=v^3$ of entries in each of the two data banks.

adds.name: invocation count
adds.meaning: The number $I=3v^2$ of separate eight-row invocations over the three stages.

adds.name: lost dimension
adds.meaning: The total label dimension lost on decreasing edges, $L_{\rm b}$ or $L_{\rm c}$ for the two networks.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values, the scalar network of three stages, each running $v^2$ separate eight-row invocations on the values that vary in one coordinate of $a\in\mathcal T^3$, sends $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ for all $N=v^3$ indices $a$ and restores every auxiliary wire; over $\mathbb F_2$ this is exactly the exchange of $X_a$ and $Y_a$.
children.method: Within one invocation cancel the old scratch contributions, copy and gather the sources into side and central wires, scatter and inject them into the targets and undo the copies, so the net change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, which equals $y\gets y+x$; then compose $y\gets y+x$, $x\gets x-y$, $y\gets y+x$ over the three stages.

motivation.text: Gathering through $h$ central wires and scattering back gives each target a low-rank summary whose coefficient depends only on the intersection size of two triples; side wires between neighboring triples subtract the unwanted coefficients, leaving the identity map, and the subtract-compute-add-undo schedule makes the outcome independent of whatever the scratch wires held.

quote.quote: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.

children.salient: Although intermediate wires hold XOR (or dyadic) combinations of data, the net effect is an exact signed exchange of the two banks and every scratch wire returns to its arbitrary initial value.

adds.name: triple set
adds.meaning: The set of three-element subsets of $[h]$; bank indices are triples of such subsets.

adds.name: first bank
adds.meaning: The data value of the $X$ bank at index $a\in\mathcal T^3$.

adds.name: second bank
adds.meaning: The data value of the $Y$ bank at index $a\in\mathcal T^3$.

children.claim: With $h=100$, $v=\binom h3=161700$, $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ and $m=h^3=1000000$, the two banks $X_a,Y_a$ are indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$; stage $j$ runs $v^2$ invocations, one per choice of the other two coordinates, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations, each with its own side wires $A_{ST}$ for neighboring ordered pairs $(S,T)$ and central wires $C_i$, $i\in[h]$ (plus $C_\ast$ in the complex construction), all with arbitrary initial values.

quote.quote: There are two data banks $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathcal T^3$.

children.claim: In the bit construction (scalars in $\mathbb F_2$, neighbors when $|S\cap T|=1$) copy adds $x_T$ to $A_{ST}$, side injection adds $\sum_{T:|S\cap T|=1}A_{ST}$ to $y_S$, gather adds $\sum_{T\ni i}x_T$ to $C_i$ and scatter adds $\sum_{i\in S}C_i$ to $y_S$; in the complex construction (scalars in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, neighbors are distinct triples with even intersection) side injection adds $-\sum_T\frac{|S\cap T|-1}2A_{ST}$, gather also adds $\sum_Tx_T$ to $C_\ast$, and scatter adds $(\sum_{i\in S}C_i-C_\ast)/2$.

quote.quote: In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$, and $S,T$ are neighbors when $|S\cap T|=1$.

children.claim: The forward schedule has eight rows (0 subtract side injection, 1 subtract scatter, 2 copy, 3 gather, 4 scatter, 5 side injection, 6 undo gather, 7 undo copy): rows $0$ and $1$ remove the effect of the old scratch values, rows $2$ to $5$ bring in the sources and add their effect to the targets, and rows $6$ and $7$ restore the scratch values.

quote.quote: The first two rows of the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values;

children.claim: With initial side and central vectors $a,c$, rows $0$ and $1$ subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$, rows $2$ and $3$ change the scratch to $a+\mathcal Vx$ and $c+\mathcal Gx$, rows $4$ and $5$ add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$ and rows $6$ and $7$ restore $a,c$, so the net target change $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ does not depend on the scratch values.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: In the bit case the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$, and the side contribution cancels it exactly at intersection one (intersections zero and two already give zero); in the complex case the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$, cancelled by the side contribution at intersections zero and two (intersection one already gives zero); in both cases the self coefficient is $1$, so the net map is $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote: In the bit case, the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$.

children.claim: Running the inverse schedule with logical source $Y$ and target $X$ gives $X\gets X-Y$, so stages $1,2,3$ take $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$, each invocation restoring its own auxiliary wires.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.claim: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}2=13968$ neighbors in the bit construction and $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}3+3\cdot97=147731$ in the complex one; counting ordered pairs ($vz$ side wires per invocation) and $c_{\rm b}=100$ or $c_{\rm c}=101$ central wires gives $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ and $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$, fixed independently of the input length.

quote.quote: All these numbers are fixed, independently of any eventual input length.

children.claim: If the scalar network is applied pointwise to arrays in $R^\Omega$ and each source, gate and sink $v$ carries an invertible frame $D_v$ (common to all incidences of a gate) with each edge from $u$ to $v$ applying $D_vD_u^{-1}$, then the common frame commutes with every pointwise linear gate, the computation implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, and for a signed role permutation the route from role $w$ to $\rho(w)$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, so only the endpoint frames determine the result and intermediate frames are free to make edges cheap.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: The vertices of either network can be labelled by nondegenerate subspaces of the $m$-dimensional space $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, nested along every edge, with terminal labels $U_a\to\mathcal F$ on $X_a$, $0\to U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$ and $0\to\mathcal F$ on scratch roles, so that the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time $3$ to time $4$, each losing $h$; hence $L=Ich$ and $\sum_e|\dim U_{\mathrm{head}(e)}-\dim U_{\mathrm{tail}(e)}|=Wm-2N+2L$.
children.method: Make neighboring triple lines orthogonal under a suitable bilinear form, expose one tensor factor of $\mathcal F$ per stage using $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}=B\perp P$, assign common gate labels by time, and tabulate the orthogonal residual of every edge.

motivation.text: A side wire joins neighboring triples, so if neighboring indicator lines are orthogonal its label can pass from $P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle$ into $P\otimes t_Y^\perp$ without shrinking; this confines every dimension decrease to the central wires, and the telescoping of signed changes then fixes the total.

quote.quote: Orthogonality of the corresponding indicator vectors permits the subspace assignments.

children.salient: Of all the edge types only the central-wire return from time $3$ to time $4$ loses dimension, so the loss is a small fixed fraction of $N$ ($100/539$ or $101/539$).

adds.name: one-factor space
adds.meaning: The label space of one triple coordinate: $\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ for the bit network, $\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product for the complex one.

adds.name: ambient label space
adds.meaning: The tensor cube $F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m$, in which every label is a nondegenerate subspace.

adds.name: source label
adds.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$, the source label of the role $X_a$.

adds.name: triple indicator
adds.meaning: The indicator vector in $F$ of a three-element subset $T$.

children.claim: For the bit network take $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ (eigenvalues $1$ and $-91/9$, hence nondegenerate), so that $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$; for the complex network take $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product, so $t_T\cdot t_T=1$; in either label field every triple line is nondegenerate and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: With $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ of dimension $m$, $U_a=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ and the prescribed terminal labels, source dimensions sum to $N$ and sink dimensions to $Wm-N$; since the label changes at a gate cancel, the signed changes sum to $Wm-2N$, and if decreasing edges lose $L$ in total the absolute changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$.

quote.quote: The source dimensions sum to $N$ and the sink dimensions to $Wm-N$.

children.claim: At stage $j$, with $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$, $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$, $B=P^\perp$ and $Q$ the line of the later factors, the $X$ label goes from $A\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $(A\otimes F)\otimes Q$ and the $Y$ label from $B\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $((B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp))\otimes Q$, exactly the next stage's incoming labels, and the gates at times $0,\dots,7$ carry the common labels $B\otimes\langle t\rangle$, $B\otimes F$, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes\langle t\rangle)$, $A\otimes F$, $B\otimes F$, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp)$, $A\otimes F$, $A\otimes F$ (each tensored by $Q$).

quote.quote: These transitions expose one tensor factor at each stage.

children.claim: With $a=h^{j-1}$ and $f=h^{3-j}$ the edge residual dimensions are: $X$ in$\to2$: $(a-1)(h-1)$; $X$ $2\to3$: $h-1$; $X$ $3\to6$, $6\to7$, $Y$ in$\to0$ and $Y$ $1\to4$: $0$; $Y$ $0\to1$: $(a-1)(h-1)$; $Y$ $4\to5$: $h-1$; center source$\to1$: $(a-1)h$; center $1\to3$, $3\to4$ and $4\to6$: $h$ each; side source$\to0$: $a-1$; side $0\to2$: $(a-1)(h-1)+1$; side $2\to5$: $h-2$ (this inclusion uses $t_X\perp t_Y$); side $5\to7$: $1$; scratch last$\to$sink: $ah(f-1)$; and label dimension decreases only on the center edge $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

quote.quote: Label dimension is nondecreasing along every edge except center $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

children.claim: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges ($c$ central wires per invocation), each losing $h$, so $L=Ich$ and replacing signed by absolute changes adds exactly $2L$ to $Wm-2N$.

quote.quote: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges, each of loss $h$; replacing signed changes by absolute changes adds $2L$.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero edge residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one vector built from coordinate units outside small supports, hence is nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis.

quote.quote: Thus every nonzero residual is nonalternating.

children.claim: With $c_{\rm b}=100$ and $c_{\rm c}=101$ central wires the loss ratios are $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both smaller than $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: In the bit network, assigning the rational projection $P_U$ (onto $U$ along $U^\perp$) to every gate or sink labelled $U$, $-P_{U_a}$ to the source of $X_a$ and $0$ to every other source gives $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ on every role and edge ranks summing to $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}=177176569088785861287000000<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Use that the difference of projections onto nested nondegenerate subspaces has rank equal to the dimension change, add the one extra rank of each negative source projection, and compute the endpoint differences.

motivation.text: Projections convert label bookkeeping into matrix ranks: for nested labels the edge matrix $P_V-P_U$ projects onto the residual, so its rank (the number of smaller interchanges the edge's address shear will cost) is the residual dimension already counted.

adds.name: label projection
adds.meaning: The rational projection onto the label $U$ along $U^\perp$, the matrix assigned to a vertex labelled $U$.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement, so its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$, and reversing an edge only negates the matrix.

quote.quote: Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections: at stage $1$ the first gate on $X_a$ has label exactly $U_a$, so its first edge matrix is $P_{U_a}-(-P_{U_a})=2P_{U_a}$, of rank one where the dimension change was zero; this adds $N$ to $Wm-2N+2L_{\rm b}$, giving $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$ with deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

quote.quote: The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections.

children.claim: For the input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has source matrix $0$ and sink matrix $I_m$, so every role's endpoint difference is $I_m$.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: In the complex network with binary labels, the phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$ make each edge change a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$ (or its inverse) per vector of an orthonormal residual basis, with $a=(1+i)/2$ and $b=(1-i)/2$, so the kernels number $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}=1873807244636671267308000000<W_{\rm c}m$, and after diagonal source and sink corrections the frames telescope to $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role.
children.method: Use additivity of Hamming weight modulo four over orthogonal binary vectors to split each frame change into one phase per residual direction, turn each phase into a translation kernel through $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$, and repair the one non-forward endpoint with $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

motivation.text: Frames that are all diagonalized by the same Hadamard matrix make every edge change a product of two-point kernels, one per residual direction, which is a smaller instance of the very $C$-layer being built, so the residual count is exactly the number of recursive calls.

quote.quote: The intermediate frames are chosen so that every edge can be implemented by smaller calls to the same procedure.

adds.name: phase exponent
adds.meaning: The function $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod4$ giving the power of $i$ on the diagonal of the frame for label $U$.

adds.name: two-point kernel
adds.meaning: The $2\times2$ matrix $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=aI+bX$, which acts on an array as a combination of the identity and a translation.

children.claim: If $V=U\perp E$ and $\mathcal B$ is an orthonormal basis of $E$, weight additivity modulo four for orthogonal binary vectors gives $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]\pmod4$ (negated on decreasing edges), and since each $\operatorname{wt}(v)$ is odd the factor $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}=\frac{1+i^\varepsilon}2+\frac{1-i^\varepsilon}2(-1)^{v\cdot x}$ becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse after Hadamard conjugation.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Summing residual basis lengths over all edges gives $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$, with deficit $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$ and no source exception, and on $k$ columns each residual vector contributes a single kernel acting on all $k$ columns.

quote.quote: The deficit is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

children.claim: The zero label has frame $I$ and the full label frame $C^{\otimes m}$; on the pair $X_a\to Y_a$ the route operator is $C^{-1}$ on the $27$ coordinates of $\operatorname{supp}(u_a)$ and $C$ elsewhere, which the wrappers $Z_{a,k}$ before and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ after turn into $C^{\otimes mk}$ by $C=iZC^{-1}Z$; negating the physical $X$ outputs and undoing $\rho$ leaves $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, scratch roles included.

quote.quote: The operator on this pair is therefore $C^{\otimes mk}$ as well.

children.claim: The relative deficits are $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$, both above $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and since $\log m<20$, $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: One fixed multitape procedure transforms any bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ by $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$ in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps, where $V=PGB\,2^{2u}$, including shape processing, padding and cleanup.
children.method: Factor each address shear into lower-triangular controlled shifts and one smaller interchange per unit of rank, run the bit network on $W_{\rm b}$ cyclic row streams to interchange chunks of $m^k$ radix-$q$ digits recursively, and reduce arbitrary widths to power widths by borrowing rows from a few high digits and padding $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$.

motivation.text: An edge matrix of rank $a$ costs $a$ smaller interchanges, so the rank deficit of the bit network turns directly into a recurrence whose solution is a power $e^\tau$, $\tau<1$, of the chunk width.

quote.quote: Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation of addresses, yet it is computed through pointwise XOR combinations of data streams, and it costs $Vu^\tau$, less than the $Vu$ of $u$ separate single-bit moves.

adds.name: radix prime
adds.meaning: A fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators of the fixed matrices; chunks are handled as radix-$q$ digit strings.

adds.name: chunk width in digits
adds.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each of the two chunks.

adds.name: first chunk
adds.meaning: The first chunk, viewed as a vector of $m$ fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$.

adds.name: second chunk
adds.meaning: The second chunk, viewed as a vector of $m$ fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ factors as $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation matrix with exactly $a$ ones, found by pivoting on the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row and clearing with lower-triangular elementary operations.

quote.quote: where $E_1,E_2$ are invertible lower triangular rational matrices and $\Pi$ has exactly $a$ entries equal to one, with at most one in each row and column

children.claim: For a fixed finite set of rational matrices there is a fixed odd prime $q$ such that, for field vectors $H,D$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with every $H_i$ before every $D_j$, the shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ for $A$ of rational rank $a$ costs exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields plus $O(V)$.
children.method: Apply $A=E_1\Pi E_2$: transform $D$ by $E_2$ and $H$ by $E_1^{-1}$ with controlled shifts, add $\Pi D$ to $H$ one pivot at a time, and transform back.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts update a later field from earlier ones in linear time, and lower-triangular changes of coordinates only ever do that, so the entire cost of the shear concentrates in the $a$ pivot additions, each of which can be traded for one interchange.

quote.quote: Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

adds.name: shear matrix
adds.meaning: A fixed rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ defining the shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$.

children.claim: Choosing an odd prime $q$ that avoids every denominator in the finite table of factors and inverses and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor makes all these rational identities hold over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with the triangular factors still invertible; the table and prime are computed once and compiled into the machine.

quote.quote: Choose an odd prime avoiding every denominator in the table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor.

children.claim: A lower-triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$: coordinates are updated in descending physical order, each multiplied by its diagonal unit and shifted by a fixed combination of earlier, still original, coordinates.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: Each one of $\Pi$ in $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ at position $(i,j)$, i.e. $H_i\gets H_i+D_j$, is done as $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, $(H_i,D_j)\gets(D_j,H_i)$, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, which sends $(h,d)$ to $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, so the number of recursive calls is exactly the rational rank $a$.

quote.quote: On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$.

children.claim: If the fixed circuit data satisfy $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ for every role and $s<Wm$, then for every $e=m^k$ two chunks of $e$ radix-$q$ digits, preceded by a row field whose length is divisible by $W^k$, are interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time for any rational $\tau\in(0,1)$ with $s/W<m^\tau$.
children.method: Split rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the circuit with frames $\Phi_M$ and implement every edge shear $\Phi_{A_e}$ by recursive interchanges of $e/m$-digit fields, merge the rows to obtain $H\gets H+D$, and solve the resulting volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Each edge shear costs as many smaller interchanges as its rank, each on a stream of volume $V/W$, so the time divided by volume grows by the factor $s/W$ per level, which the rank saving keeps below $m^\tau$.

quote.quote: A recursive call at parameter $mf$ therefore uses $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on a stream of volume $V/W$.

children.salient: Every role stream, including those that began as arbitrary scratch rows, ends with exactly the same shear $H\gets H+D$, so the rows can simply be merged back into place.

adds.name: recursion depth
adds.meaning: The exponent with $e=m^k$, the number of levels of the recursion.

adds.name: normalized cost
adds.meaning: A uniform bound on the time divided by logical volume for interchanging chunks of $m^k$ digits.

adds.name: shear frame
adds.meaning: The array permutation moving the entry at address $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$.

adds.name: edge matrix
adds.meaning: The difference $M_{\mathrm{head}(e)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(e)}$ of the matrices at the ends of edge $e$.

children.claim: The bit-network interface supplies the contract $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ for $1\le w\le W$ and $s=\sum_e\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}A_e<Wm$ with $A_e=M_{\mathrm{head}(e)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(e)}$, $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$, the negative source projections being already included in the rank sum.

quote.quote: Proposition~\ref{prop:bit-motif-interface} supplies these conditions with $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$.

children.claim: For $k>0$ each chunk is written as $m$ fields of $b=e/m$ digits, giving $H,D$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$, and whole rows are split cyclically, row $Wg+(w-1)$ to stream $w$, into $W$ role streams of identical shape and volume $V/W$, each with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: With the frame $\Phi_M$ moving the entry at $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$, so that $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$, applying $\Phi_{A_e}$ on each edge and the gates pointwise gives $f'_{\rho(w)}=\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$, and returning row $g$ of role $\rho(w)$ to row $Wg+(w-1)$ yields $H\gets H+D$ on every original row, scratch rows included.

quote.quote: The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The full interchange is $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ componentwise, which sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$; only the middle shear uses the circuit, the other two being linear controlled updates.

quote.quote: Only the middle shear uses the circuit.

children.claim: The recursive calls number exactly $s$, each on a role stream of volume $V/W$, while splitting, merging, gates and triangular operations cost $O(V)$ per node, so the normalized cost satisfies $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$; with $s/W<m^\tau$ the geometric sum $\sum_{j\le k}(s/W)^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$, hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: A fixed-tape depth-first schedule ($W$ role tapes, one parking stack for the $W-1$ inactive streams, a descriptor stack) moves only $O(V)$ symbols per node for the fixed number $s$ of children, and descriptor work is $(\log(2V_0))^{O(1)}=O(V_j)$ because both chunk ranges stay present in every child, so temporary storage never replaces logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

quote.quote: Temporary storage is therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

children.claim: For chunk ranges $[q^e]$ take $k=\lceil\log_me\rceil$ and use the top $\rho=\lceil k\log W/(2\log q)\rceil=O(\log(2e))$ digits of both chunks as a row field of range $R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$, padded with zero rows to $R'<2R$; writing $e-\rho=\sum_ja_jm^j$ with $0\le a_j<m$, the power-width pieces are interchanged at total cost $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$, because $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$, while moving the high digits costs $O(V\log(2e))$.

quote.quote: The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: For binary chunks let $e$ be least with $q^e\ge2^u$ and pad both ranges numerically from $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ (volume grows by less than $q^2$, and lexicographic radix-$q$ order is numerical order), so the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$ since $e=O(u)$.

quote.quote: Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.claim: For $p\ge p_0$, $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$, $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ and $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$, one fixed procedure applies the tensor product $\mathcal H$ of $H_0$ on bit $\rho$ of each of $D\le d$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks of an array on $[P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S]$ whose records are disk-valued polynomials with $r$ coefficients on $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$, returning $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$ in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time with $\|Q_p(\mathcal Hz)-\mathcal Hz\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, every value being an exact Gaussian dyadic until one final truncation.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, build $C^{\otimes e}$ recursively from the complex network with phase frames on $m$ slots of $e/m$ chunks, realize the binary changes of basis by packed selected-bit additions, distribute rows among the $W$ roles to shrink each call's volume, and bound the growth of exact intermediate values.

motivation.text: Separate butterfly factors would cost $D$ whole-array passes; the phase frames instead reduce a $C$-layer on $e$ chunks to $s$ layers on $e/m$ chunks separated by binary basis changes, and those basis changes are cheap address operations.

quote.quote: Its phase frames express a $C$ tensor product using smaller groups of selected bits, separated by binary changes of basis.

children.salient: The layer acts on all $D$ selected axes for less than one pass per axis, $d^{\lambda'}$ with $\lambda'<1$, and although its intermediate operators are not contractions it is evaluated exactly with only $o(p)$ extra bits.

adds.name: working precision

adds.name: axis exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent with $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$; the algorithm takes $\epsilon=2^{-75}$.

adds.name: axis bound
adds.meaning: An upper bound on the number of selected chunks, $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$; the algorithm takes $d=\lfloor b^\epsilon\rfloor$.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ of address bits in each axis chunk.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, a power of two with $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$.

adds.name: selected chunks
adds.meaning: The number $1\le D\le d$ of consecutive chunks whose selected bit the layer acts on.

adds.name: group size
adds.meaning: The number of active chunks handled by one recursive call.

adds.name: butterfly layer
adds.meaning: The tensor product of $H_0$ over the selected bits, acting coefficientwise on every record.

adds.name: truncation
adds.meaning: Componentwise truncation toward zero of real and imaginary parts to the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z$.

children.claim: With $C=H\mathsf SH=aI+bX$, an edge from $U_-$ to $U_+$ with orthonormal residual basis $v_1,\dots,v_{\rho_{\rm edge}}$ is applied to a group of $e=mf$ chunks, divided into $m$ slots of $f$ chunks, by a binary change of basis $\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ on every column, one child $(C^{\pm1})^{\otimes f}$ on each of the first $\rho_{\rm edge}$ slots, and $\mathcal P_M$ back, so one network invocation makes exactly $s_{\rm c}$ forward children on $e/m$ chunks and yields $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role, and finally $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$.
children.method: Conjugate translation kernels $X_v$ into coordinate kernels $X_{e_j}$ by an invertible binary matrix, realize that matrix by elementary row additions on whole slots, convert inverse kernels with $Z$ wrappers, and reach $H_0$ through diagonal phases.

motivation.text: Expressing each edge's residual operator as two-point kernels on coordinate directions makes every edge a set of smaller simultaneous $C$-layers on single slots, separated only by binary changes of address basis, which are cheap packed address operations.

quote.quote: The phase identities below express an edge's residual operator as a product of two-point kernels on selected directions.

children.salient: Inverse kernels and all endpoint corrections cost no extra recursive call: $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}$ is one forward call wrapped in address signs and a fourth-root phase.

adds.name: slot width
adds.meaning: The number of chunks in each of the $m$ slots of a group, $f=e/m$.

adds.name: residual dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension of an edge's orthogonal residual, the number of its directional kernels.

adds.name: basis change
adds.meaning: The address permutation moving the value at $x$ to $Mx$ for an invertible binary matrix $M$.

children.claim: Direct multiplication gives $H_0=b\mathsf SC\mathsf S$, $C^2=X$, $C^4=I$ and $C^{-1}=bI+aX=-iZCZ$, all with Gaussian dyadic coefficients; the Hadamard matrices serve only in proofs and are never executed.

quote.quote: These identities use only Gaussian dyadic coefficients.

children.claim: For $M\in\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ whose first $\rho_{\rm edge}$ columns are the residual basis, $\mathcal P_MX_v\mathcal P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}$ gives $\mathcal C_{U_+}\mathcal C_{U_-}^{-1}=\mathcal P_M(\prod_jC_{e_j}^{\epsilon_j})\mathcal P_M^{-1}$, which uses only the invertibility of $M$.

quote.quote: The matrix $M$ need not preserve the dot product: equation~\eqref{eq:phase-conjugation} only uses its invertibility.

children.claim: On the group, column $j$ is $(x_{1,j},\dots,x_{m,j})$; apply $\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ to each column, $(C^{\epsilon_h})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ selected bits of slot $h\le\rho_{\rm edge}$, and $\mathcal P_M$ back, where $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$ makes every child a forward call.

quote.quote: A negative directional kernel still requires only one forward child, because

quote.quote: Gaussian elimination expresses any $M\in\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ as a product of at most $m(m-1)+3m$ elementary row additions:

children.claim: Summing residual dimensions over one invocation on $e=mf$ axes gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls on $f=e/m$ axes, and the $Z_{a,f}$ signs with the scalar $i^{27f}$ produce $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role, roles with arbitrary initial scratch values included.

quote.quote: Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.

children.claim: With $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\cdots+x_D}z(x)$, $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ and $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a binary shift and a fourth-root phase with at most one further factor $b$, so the whole parallel butterfly layer is exact up to its final truncation.

quote.quote: so it is a binary shift and fourth-root phase, with at most one further factor $b$.

children.claim: On $R$-bit records over $[N_0]\times[2^L]_{\chi_1}\times[N_1]\times[2^L]_{\chi_2}\times[N_2]\times[2^L]_{\chi_3}\times[N_3]$ with $L=fK$, one fixed procedure performs $y_{j_i}\gets y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$ at $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, restoring the scratch chunk $z$ for every initial value, in time $O(V(L^\tau+1)+MA_{\rm rect}^3+\delta_{\rm bad}MA_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$ with $\delta_{\rm bad}=\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$, which is $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ when $A_{\rm rect}=O(p)$, $R$ exceeds every fixed polynomial in $p$, $f\le d\le p$ and $K/\log p\to\infty$.
children.method: Perform eight packed modular additions, each a single cyclic shift of a whole chunk range done between chunk interchanges, which agree with the ideal XOR except on addresses whose guard values lie near the segment ends, then repair exactly those addresses by an explicit sort.

motivation.text: Packing all $f$ segment additions into one cyclic shift of a chunk costs linear time, and carries can spoil only an $O(f2^{-K})$ fraction of addresses determined by address bits alone, so a deterministic sort of that small set restores exactness whatever the data.

quote.quote: The correction depends only on addresses, so the time bound is worst-case over all payloads.

children.salient: A permutation of address bits is obtained from integer additions on addresses, and the exceptional set is explicit and independent of the payload, so the bound is deterministic worst case.

adds.name: selected positions
adds.meaning: The number of selected bit positions in each chunk, one per $K$-bit axis chunk.

adds.name: chunk bit width
adds.meaning: The number $L=fK$ of address bits in each of the chunks $x,y,z$.

adds.name: bad set
adds.meaning: The addresses at which some guard value lies within ten of the end of its range.

adds.name: bad fraction
adds.meaning: The bound $\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$ on the fraction of exceptional addresses.

adds.name: record count
adds.meaning: The number of records in the rectangle.

adds.name: address length
adds.meaning: The bit length $\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil$ bounding every address and descriptor integer.

adds.name: record width
adds.meaning: The number of payload bits in each record.

children.claim: For a Boolean control $c$ and integers $u,w$, the eight updates induce the cycle $(00\ 01\ 10)$ and then $(01\ 10\ 11)$ on parity pairs, composing to $(00\ 10)(01\ 11)$, so $(u',w')=(u+c(1-2(u\bmod2)),w)$: the parity of $u$ flips exactly when $c=1$, both halves are kept, $w$ is restored, and each coordinate moves by at most four.

quote.quote: Thus the parity of $u$ is flipped precisely when $c=1$, both quotients under division by two are preserved, and the arbitrary auxiliary integer $w$ is restored.

children.claim: Taking the $K$-bit segments starting at $j_i$, $i<f-1$, of $y$ and $z$ as $u_i=2g_i+a_i$ and $w_i=2h_i+b_i$ with control $c_i=x_{j_i}$, each of the eight lines on all segments at once is the single cyclic shift $y\gets y+\varepsilon\sum_i2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b]\pmod{2^L}$, whose offset never depends on its target chunk, so each line is a bijection.

quote.quote: The shift offset never depends on its target chunk, so each line is a bijection of the rectangle.

children.claim: Outside the set $\mathcal B$ of addresses where some guard value fails $10\le g\le2^{K-1}-11$, a displacement of at most eight never carries between segments, so the composition $S_0$ of the shifts equals the ideal map $T_0$; with twenty excluded values per guard out of $2^{K-1}$ and $2(f-1)$ guards, $|\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M$ independently of the record values.

quote.quote: There are exactly twenty excluded values for each guard in

children.claim: Since $T_0$ preserves guard values, $S_0(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B$ and $T_0S_0^{-1}$ permutes $\mathcal B$; the procedure does the rotations between at most sixteen chunk swaps, extracts the records of $\mathcal B$ with their destination ranks, stable-radix-sorts only those and reinserts them, and finally XORs the omitted top position $j_{f-1}$ directly.

quote.quote: Thus $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

children.claim: Movement costs $O(V(L^\tau+1))$, full record scans $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3+V)$ and at most $A_{\rm rect}$ radix passes over the exceptional records $O(|\mathcal B|A_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$; divided by $V=MR$ the extra terms are $A_{\rm rect}^3/R\to0$ and $O(p^22^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$ under the family bounds.

quote.quote: Under the stated family bounds the first tends to zero, and the second is $O(p^2 2^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$.

children.claim: In one invocation on $e=mf$ axes a row addition uses slot $h'$ as $x$, slot $h$ as $y$ and any third slot as $z$, so a complete binary change of basis and its inverse cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ on a stream of volume $V$, also after row padding and splitting.

quote.quote: the complete change of basis and its inverse therefore cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ on a stream of volume $V$.

children.claim: If $F(e)$ denotes the layer time on $e$ active chunks divided by the current volume, then $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ at internal nodes and $F(e)=O(e)$ for $e<d^\beta$, and with rows supplied by $q_0$ leading chunks and a base-$m$ partition of the rest the layer costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for $\max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Charge a leaf $e$ individual kernels and an internal node its basis changes and gates, give each of the $s$ children $1/W$ of the volume by splitting rows among the roles, and sum the geometric series over the levels and the base-$m$ pieces.

motivation.text: Splitting complete rows among the $W$ roles gives each of the $s$ children only $1/W$ of the parent's volume, so after dividing by volume the recursion grows by the factor $s/W<m^\sigma$ per level, the complex counterpart of the interchange recurrence.

quote.quote: Splitting complete rows among the network's wire roles then reduces the volume of each recursive call.

children.salient: The overhead $(eK)^\tau$ stays below $e^\lambda$ only because recursion stops at $e<d^{1/2}$ and the chunk width $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ is a tiny power of $d$.

adds.name: stopping exponent
adds.meaning: Recursion stops when a group has fewer than $d^\beta$ chunks; $\beta=1/2$.

adds.name: overhead exponent
adds.meaning: A fixed exponent with $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1$ and $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda$; the algorithm takes $\lambda=1-2^{-52}$.

adds.name: chunk exponent
adds.meaning: The exponent in $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$; the algorithm takes $c=2^{-56}$.

adds.name: row chunks
adds.meaning: The number $\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ of leading chunks used as a row index.

adds.name: maximal depth
adds.meaning: The number $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ bounding the recursion depth.

children.claim: One $C$ kernel on one selected bit splits the stream on that bit into two aligned streams, computes $C(u,v)=(\frac{u+v+i(u-v)}2,\frac{u+v-i(u-v)}2)$ coefficientwise at the common exact width and merges, in $O(V)$, so $e$ individual kernels cost $O(Ve)$.

quote.quote: Thus \(e\) individual kernels cost \(O(Ve)\) on any stream with these complete ranges and record format.

children.claim: At an internal node with $e=m^k$ active chunks split into $m$ slots of $e/m$ chunks, one network invocation makes exactly $s$ recursive calls, while basis changes, inverses, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$, the number of row additions being fixed.

quote.quote: The phase construction supplies one recursive call on a slot for each vector in an edge residual basis, hence exactly \(s\) calls in one invocation of the network.

children.claim: With $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ and $k_0=\lceil\log_md\rceil$, the first $q_0$ chunks are processed by individual kernels in $O(V\log d)$ and then serve as a row index of range $2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}$, padded with zero rows to a multiple of $W^{k_0}$ at most doubling the volume (if $D\le q_0$ individual kernels do everything).

quote.quote: If \(D\le q_0\), use individual \(C\) kernels, at cost \(O(V\log d)\).

children.claim: At a node, row $Wg+w$ goes to role $w$, so all role streams share the remaining address shape, scratch roles are supplied by existing rows, and each recursive edge call acts on a stream of exactly $1/W$ of its parent's volume.

quote.quote: Each recursive edge call acts on one role stream with volume exactly \(1/W\) of its parent's logical volume.

children.claim: Choosing $0<\tau<1$, $\log_m(s/W)\le\sigma<1$, $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1$ and $\tau(1+c/\beta)<\lambda$ with $\beta=1/2$, the $s$ children cost $s(V/W)F(e/m)$, internal overhead is $O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)$ because $K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}$ at internal nodes and sums to $O(e^\lambda)$ over the levels, and leaves after $j$ levels contribute $O(a^ju)\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)})$ using $a^j\le m^{j\sigma}=(e/u)^\sigma$ for $a=s/W$.

quote.quote: Dividing by the current volume \(V\) gives the factor \(s/W\).

children.claim: Writing $D-q_0=\sum_ja_jm^j$ gives at most $(m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_md\rfloor)$ pieces, so the total normalized cost is $O(\log(2d)[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1])=O(d^{\lambda'})$.

quote.quote: There are at most \((m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_m d\rfloor)\) pieces.

children.claim: Every intermediate coefficient of one accelerated layer is an exact Gaussian dyadic using at most $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer and sign bits per real component, where $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$, $C_0=128mB^2$, $B=s+E$, $E=64(W+m+1)^3$ and $C_1=20$, and the choice $\epsilon C_1<1$ makes $\Delta=o(p)$, so the coefficient width stays $O(p)$.
children.method: Bound the arithmetic dependency depth $A(e)$ of any coefficient by a recurrence over the network recursion, then use that depth $\ell$ costs at most $\ell$ denominator bits and a factor $2^\ell$ in modulus.

motivation.text: The frames and kernels inside the network may enlarge values, so contraction arguments cannot bound intermediate sizes; counting the longest chain of additions and halvings bounds denominators and magnitudes together.

quote.quote: Its intermediate operators need not be contractions.

children.salient: Although the network has more than $10^{21}$ wires, the extra bits grow only like the fixed power $d^{20}$ of the axis count, which is $o(p)$.

adds.name: invocation depth
adds.meaning: The bound $64(W+m+1)^3$ on the arithmetic depth added by the gates and corrections of one network invocation.

adds.name: depth growth
adds.meaning: The per-level depth multiplier $s+E$.

adds.name: depth exponent
adds.meaning: The least $j\ge1$ with $m^j\ge B$; here $\nu=11$.

adds.name: guard constant
adds.meaning: The constant $128mB^2$.

adds.name: guard exponent
adds.meaning: The exponent $\max\{20,\nu+3\}=20$ in the guard width.

adds.name: guard width
adds.meaning: The number $\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$ of extra fractional and integer bits reserved per real component.

adds.name: dependency depth
adds.meaning: $A(e)$ bounds the number of arithmetic operations on any chain from an input coefficient to an intermediate coefficient of a $C$-layer on $e$ chunks.

quote.quote: These values give \(m^{10}<B<m^{11}\), hence \(\nu=11\) and \(C_1=20\).

children.claim: Each wire meets at most twelve scalar gates, so an invocation has at most $12W$ gates, each evaluated in at most $2W^2$ operations, plus at most $4s$ operations for inverse-child corrections and $4W+4$ for source, sink and bank corrections; the total $24W^3+4s+4W+4$ is below $E$.

quote.quote: Since \(s<Wm\), the total \(24W^3+4s+4W+4\) is less than \(E=64(W+m+1)^3\).

children.method: Compute both forward synthetic transforms in the retained layout, multiply corresponding polynomial records by signed Kronecker packing with the $O(N\log N)$ multiplier, apply the opposite synthetic transform to that same order, and scale exactly by $M$.

motivation.text: Both forward outputs are stored in the same permuted order and pointwise products commute with a common record permutation, so no reordering is executed and the opposite transform is built to consume that order.

children.claim: In $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, $r$ a power of two, with the coefficient sup norm, multiplication by $y^a$ permutes the coefficients and changes some signs, so it is an isometry, and truncation $Q_p$ to the grid satisfies $\|Q_pz-z\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ and $\|Q_pz\|_\infty\le\|z\|_\infty$.

quote.quote: Multiplication by $y^a$, for any integer $a$, permutes the coefficients and changes some signs; consequently it is an isometry for this norm.

children.claim: For a power of two $t$ dividing $2r$ and $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$, the transforms $(F_t^\mp z)_j=\frac1t\sum_k\omega_t^{\mp jk}z_k$ on $\mathcal R_r^t$ are contractions with $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$, and $F_t^-$ is computed by $\log_2t$ levels of $H_0$ butterflies whose twiddle factors $\omega_t^{-k}$ are signed coefficient shifts.
children.method: Verify character cancellation directly in the ring and run the radix-two decimation-in-frequency recursion with polynomial roots of unity.

motivation.text: Using powers of $y$ as roots of unity makes every twiddle multiplication an exact signed shift of the coefficient list, so the only arithmetic left in a transform is its butterflies, which the simultaneous layer accelerates.

quote.quote: Their entries will be short polynomials in a quotient where the required roots of unity act by exact signed permutations of coefficient lists.

children.salient: Twiddle multiplications cost no arithmetic and introduce no rounding; only the butterflies compute.

adds.name: polynomial root
adds.meaning: The element $y^{2r/t}$ of $\mathcal R_r$, a principal $t$-th root of unity.

adds.name: synthetic transform
adds.meaning: The normalized length-$t$ transform over $\mathcal R_r$ with root $\omega_t$, written $F_t^-$ or $F_t^+$ by sign.

children.claim: Every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry and each transform entry averages $t$ such images, so both $F_t^-$ and $F_t^+$ are contractions.

quote.quote: Thus both transforms are contractions.

children.claim: Because $\mathcal R_r$ has zero divisors, character cancellation is checked directly: for $t\nmid j$ with $j=2^vj_0$, shifting $k$ by $t/2^{v+1}$ multiplies the sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$, so $\sum_k\omega_t^{jk}$ is $t$ if $t\mid j$ and $0$ otherwise, which gives $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$.

quote.quote: Hence the sum is zero, since the additive group of $\mathcal R_r$ has no two-torsion.

children.claim: For $t\ge2$ the decimation-in-frequency step applies $H_0$ to each pair $(z_k,z_{k+t/2})$, multiplies the $b=1$ output by $\omega_t^{-k}$ and recurses on both halves, because $(F_t^-z)_{2h+b}=\frac1{t/2}\sum_{k<t/2}(\omega_t^2)^{-hk}\omega_t^{-bk}\frac{z_k+(-1)^bz_{k+t/2}}2$.

quote.quote: the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$ for $0\leq k<t/2$.

children.claim: After all $a=\log_2t$ levels the entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ sits in slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$, so the forward recursion implements $B_tF_t^-$ without moving frequency indices, and the reversed recursion (inverse monomial, then $H_0$, each level half the inverse of the forward level since $H_0^2=I/2$) implements $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$, consuming that stored order.

quote.quote: The recursion writes its outputs directly in this order; it does not move whole frequency indices.

children.salient: The forward and opposite transforms meet in the same scrambled order, so the bit-reversal permutation is never executed.

children.claim: For $D$ axes with $F_{\boldsymbol t}^\pm=\bigotimes_iF_{t_i}^\pm$ and $B=\bigotimes_iB_{t_i}$, the axis steps of one round commute and group into a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$ followed by one recordwise monomial $J_E$, multiplication by $y^E$ with $E=-\sum_i\frac{2r}{u_i}b_ik_i\pmod{2r}$ depending only on the address, so every round is a contraction.

quote.quote: Consequently the individual axis steps may be grouped as a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$, followed by one recordwise monomial operation $J_E$.

children.claim: For $d\ge2$, $r=2^\ell$, $d\ell\le C_\ell p$, $1\le K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor\le\ell-1$ and $d-1$ axes of lengths $t_i\in\{2^{\ell-1},2^\ell\}$, a layout permutation $L$ of record addresses lets the forward procedure compute $LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and the opposite procedure $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$, each with error less than $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$, in time $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
children.method: Move the leading and low bit slots of every axis to a prefix, interleave the remaining $K$-bit chunks so that equal-index chunks of all axes are consecutive, run each remaining round as one simultaneous layer and each prefix round axis by axis, and truncate once per round.

motivation.text: The simultaneous layer accepts one bit at a common offset in each of $D$ consecutive equal chunks, so the transform's address bits must first be arranged in that pattern, and the chunk interchange makes this rearrangement cheap.

quote.quote: we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.claim: With $(\ell-1)\bmod K$ low slots and $\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$ remaining $K$-bit chunks per axis, moving the leading slot of each long axis and the low slots of every axis to a prefix takes $O(dK)$ single-bit moves costing $O(TpdK)$.

quote.quote: There are at most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$ listed slots, so the moves cost $O(TpdK)$.

children.claim: Reordering the remaining chunks from axis-major to chunk-index-major order takes at most $D\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor-1$ exchanges of width-$K$ chunks, each $O(TpK^\tau)$ by the chunk interchange, in total $O(Tp\,pK^{\tau-1})$.

quote.quote: This uses at most $Dq-1$ exchanges of width-$K$ address chunks, even when the chunks are nonadjacent.

children.claim: In a round on the remaining chunks the selected bit has one common offset in each of the $D$ consecutive chunks of one chunk index, the layer sees a complete address set $[P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S]$ with $\log_2(2M)\le C_Mp$ and an $O(p)$-bit header, so the simultaneous layer costs $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ for all rounds.

quote.quote: The simultaneous-layer procedure therefore applies at cost $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total.

children.claim: At most $K$ rounds on prefix slots are done axis by axis with exact half-sums and half-differences, needing only $p+D+O(1)$ bits per component, at cost $O(TpdK)$.

quote.quote: There are at most $b+1\leq K$ rounds on prefix slots, giving cost $O(TpdK)$.

children.claim: The monomial $J_E$ is a split, exchange and sign change of each coefficient list in $O(rp)$ per record, its exponent computed from address bits in $\operatorname{poly}(p)$ time absorbed because $r$ dominates every fixed power of $p$; as truncation toward zero is odd and componentwise, $J_EQ_p(\mathcal Hz)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal Hz)$, so each round is one exact contraction followed by one truncation adding less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, and at most $\ell$ rounds give error less than $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Thus the actual forward call sequence returns exactly the result of truncating once after the exact contraction round.

children.claim: Executing the logical procedures on slots relocated by $L$ conjugates them by $L$, so the full exact operators are $(L\mathcal D_-L^{-1})L=LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and $L^{-1}(L\mathcal D_+L^{-1})=F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$, and the forward entry with frequency $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.

quote.quote: In particular, the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.

children.claim: For $r=2^\ell<2^p$ and disk-grid $f,g\in\mathcal R_r$, the exact Gaussian integer numerators of $fg$, and then $Q_p(fg/r)$ with error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, are computed in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time by evaluating four integer coefficient polynomials at $B_0=2^{4p}$, multiplying four pairs with the established $O(N\log N)$ multiplier and extracting the coefficients.
children.method: Signed Kronecker substitution: pack each real or imaginary numerator polynomial into one signed integer of $4p$-bit blocks, multiply, unpack by centered residues, then combine into real and imaginary parts, reduce modulo $y^r+1$ and truncate.

motivation.text: Four integer products of $O(rp)$ bits cost $O(rp\log(rp))$ with an already established multiplier, only $\log(rp)=O(p^{1-\epsilon})$ per bit, so the short polynomial products need no new fast algorithm and never call the one being built.

adds.name: packing base
adds.meaning: The radix $2^{4p}$ at which the coefficient polynomials are evaluated.

quote.quote: shows that each magnitude fits in $4pr$ bits.

children.claim: Every coefficient of these products satisfies $|h_j|\le r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2$, so once lower coefficients are removed the next is its centered residue modulo $B_0$; a carry in $\{0,1\}$ extracts all coefficients in $O(rp)$, the final carry cancelling the sign extension of a negative product.

quote.quote: this strict bound identifies the next coefficient by its centered residue modulo $B_0$.

children.claim: The numerators $ac-be$ and $ae+bc$ are reduced modulo $y^r+1$ by subtracting the coefficient at $j+r$ from that at $j$, giving $|H_j|\le r2^{2p}$, and shifting each part right by $p+\ell$ bits gives $Q_p(fg/r)$; four exact integer products dominate the linear costs.

quote.quote: Four exact integer products dominate the linear packing, extraction, combination, wrapping, and truncation costs.

children.claim: Since $F_{\boldsymbol t}^-(f*g)=M(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f)(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+F_{\boldsymbol t}^-=I/M$, $MF_{\boldsymbol t}^+((F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f)(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)/r)=(f*g)/(rM)$, and the pointwise product $P(u,v)=uv/r$ satisfies $P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)$, so the opposite procedure on the stored products followed by exact scaling by $M$ gives $\mathcal M_r(f,g)$.

quote.quote: Since $LB$ permutes records and leaves their polynomial suffixes intact, $P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)$.

children.claim: With forward errors below $\delta=\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ and truncation error $\eta=\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, bilinearity and the disk bounds give a product error below $2\delta+\eta$ and, after the contractive opposite transform, below $3\delta+\eta$; scaling by $M$ gives $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, and the $M$ products of cost $O(rp\log(rp))$ give the $\log(rp)$ term.

quote.quote: The final exact multiplication by $M$ therefore gives error less than $M(3\delta+\eta)=\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, as claimed.

children.claim: For distinct odd primes $s_i<t_i$ with $t_i$ powers of two and $S=\prod_is_i$, the prime-length transform with its source permutation, $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, equals $2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with Gaussian contractions $\mathcal A,\mathcal B_0$; the middle factor $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ is a chirp-conjugated cyclic convolution; and the retained permutation $R$ cancels in $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$, so neither permutation is ever executed.
children.method: Adapt Harvey and van der Hoeven's Gaussian resampling identity keeping both coordinate permutations inside it, express the permuted power-of-two transform through Bluestein's chirp identity, and check that the source permutation cancels across a convolution.

motivation.text: The Chinese-remainder split needs pairwise coprime axis lengths while the synthetic transforms need powers of two; resampling bridges the two shapes, and computing the identity with its permutations left in place avoids sorting.

quote.quote: The transform lengths needed for the integer product are pairwise coprime, whereas the synthetic transforms use powers of two. Gaussian resampling connects these two shapes.

quote.quote: Composing such algorithms adds their errors: at each step, insert the exact map at the computed input and use its contraction bound on the accumulated input error.

motivation.text: The usual implementation sorts twice per coordinate, at $O(tp\log t)$ each, which would already cost a full logarithm; keeping both permutations inside the identity removes those sorts, and they later cancel or are absorbed by the chirp.

quote.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.

children.claim: Exposing an axis as the innermost field and restoring it takes $O(d)$ adjacent interchanges of $\ell$- or $(\ell-1)$-bit fields, each $O(Tp(1+\ell^\tau))$, so all axes cost $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$, and per-line setup of $O(p^c)$ totals $O(dTp^c/r)=o(Tp)$.

quote.quote: Exposing and restoring one axis needs $O(d)$ adjacent interchanges, hence all axes need $O(d^2)$.

children.claim: If every $t_i$ is even and $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp(-\pi i\sum_is_ij_i^2/t_i)$, then $a$ has period $t_i$ in coordinate $i$ and $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot u)}T$, because the coefficient $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}=\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$ is that of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, which reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform.

quote.quote: This is precisely the coefficient in $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, because $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_i j_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform.

children.claim: Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, so $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=R^{-1}F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ and $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$; since a coordinate permutation commutes with pointwise products, $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, this yields $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$, and conjugating input and output turns an algorithm for $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ into one for $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.

quote.quote: Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, so tensoring this identity gives $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=R^{-1}F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ and hence $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.

children.claim: For large $n$ there are distinct odd primes $s_1,\dots,s_d$ with $(1-2\eta)t_i<s_i\le(1-\eta)t_i$, found deterministically in $n^{o(1)}$ time, such that $T/2<S<T$ for $S=\prod_is_i$ and every pair $(s_i,t_i)$ meets the hypotheses of one-dimensional resampling.
children.method: Count primes in the two intervals with the explicit prime-interval estimate, multiply the lower bounds, check the separation $\alpha^4\theta_i>p$, and bound the cost of a trial-division search.

motivation.text: The prime lengths must be close to the powers of two in both directions: near enough that their product fills a fixed fraction of the padded box, far enough that each ratio leaves the separation resampling needs.

quote.quote: their product must occupy a fixed fraction of the padded box, while each ratio $t_i/s_i$ must leave enough separation for resampling.

adds.meaning: The relative margin $1/(4d)$ below each $t_i$ inside which $s_i$ is chosen.

children.claim: Bernoulli's inequality gives $S/T>(1-\frac1{2d})^d>\frac12$, hence $T/2<S<T$, and $\theta_i=t_i/s_i-1>\eta$ gives $\alpha^4\theta_i>12d^2b/(4d)=3db\ge6b=p$; with $t_i\le r\le T<2^p$, every resampling hypothesis holds.

quote.quote: Together with $s_i<t_i$, this gives $T/2<S<T$.

children.claim: Scanning both intervals with trial division costs $O(dr^{3/2}\operatorname{poly}(p))$, whose logarithm is $O(\log p+p/d)=o(p)$, i.e. $n^{o(1)}=o(n)$ time, so the primes and all length parameters are computed by the machine rather than supplied as advice.

quote.quote: All primes and length parameters are therefore generated by the machine; they are not advice.

children.claim: Writing each input as a polynomial in $2^b$ with $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ nonnegative digits, the product has degree at most $2q-2<2n/b\le T/2<S$, so convolution modulo $x^S-1$ has no nonzero wraparound, and every coefficient satisfies $0\le c_j\le q(2^b-1)^2<2^{3b}$ since $q\le n\le2^b$.

quote.quote: Thus convolution modulo $x^S-1$ has no nonzero wraparound.

children.claim: With $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\bmod s_i$, the map $\Phi:x\mapsto\prod_ix_i^{\mu_i}$ is an algebra isomorphism from $\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)$ onto $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^{s_1}-1,\dots,x_d^{s_d}-1)$ preserving cyclic convolution, and $\Phi$, its inverse and their padding into the box $\prod_i[0,t_i)$ cost $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$.
children.method: Write coefficient indices in mixed radix so each target coordinate is a triangular function of earlier digits, and realize the change of order by a padding scan, axis reversal through chunk interchanges, and prefix-controlled cyclic shifts.

motivation.text: Choosing the coordinate powers $\mu_i$ makes the new coordinate of axis $i$ depend only on digits before it, so the whole change of order is a sequence of controlled cyclic shifts, each linear time on tape.

quote.quote: with coordinate powers that make the change of order a sequence of controlled cyclic shifts.

adds.name: CRT exponent
adds.meaning: The inverse of $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ modulo $s_i$.

children.claim: $\Phi$ respects $x^S=1$, and the image of $x$ has order $S$ because each $\mu_i$ is a unit and the $s_i$ are pairwise coprime, so its powers run through all $S$ target monomials once and $\Phi$ is an isomorphism preserving cyclic convolution.

quote.quote: Hence $\Phi$ is an isomorphism and preserves cyclic convolution.

children.claim: For $k=\sum_ja_jP_j$ with $0\le a_j<s_j$, the axis-$i$ coordinate of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $b_i=a_i+\mu_i\sum_{j<i}a_jP_j\pmod{s_i}$, because terms with $j>i$ are divisible by $s_i$ and $\mu_iP_i\equiv1$.

quote.quote: Indeed terms with $j>i$ are divisible by $s_i$, and $\mu_iP_i=1$ modulo $s_i$.

children.claim: One nested scan inserts the zero padding, the axes are reordered to $(a_1,\dots,a_d)$, and targets are updated for $i=d,\dots,1$ by rotating the valid interval $[0,s_i)$ and fixing $[s_i,t_i)$, a bijection of the box that preserves the valid set so padding stays zero, with offsets prepared in $O(dTp^C/r)=o(Tp)$.

quote.quote: Consequently zero padding remains zero after every step.

children.claim: Reversing all axes uses $O(d^2)$ moves of adjacent axes, each an equal-width chunk interchange plus a fixed number of linear passes, so $\Phi$, its inverse and their padding cost $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$.

quote.quote: Reversing all axes uses $O(d^2)$ such moves.

children.claim: With $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$, the twist $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$ is an isometric isomorphism $\mathbb C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1)\to\mathcal R_r$, so normalized complex cyclic convolution on all $d$ axes is $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)=D_-\iota^{-1}\mathcal M_r(\iota D_+f,\iota D_+g)=(f*g)/T$, and its computed version with disk-grid phases of error below $2\,2^{-p}$ adds only $O(Tp^{1+\delta})$ to the ring convolution.
children.method: Check that the negacyclic sign cancels the twist on every wrapped product term, then apply the twist linewise and identify the last axis with the polynomial coefficient list.

motivation.text: The ring convolution wraps the last coordinate with a minus sign; multiplying coefficient $k$ by $\zeta^k$ with $\zeta^r=-1$ gives every wrapped term a second minus sign, so untwisting recovers exactly the cyclic convolution.

quote.quote: its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.

children.salient: The two signs cancel exactly: the twist contributes $\zeta^r=-1$ and the negacyclic reduction contributes $-1$ on every wrapped term.

adds.name: twist root
adds.meaning: The primitive $2r$-th root of unity $e^{\pi i/r}$.

adds.name: record identification
adds.meaning: The map viewing the last scalar axis of length $r$ as the coefficient list of a polynomial in $\mathcal R_r$.

children.claim: $\Theta:x_d\mapsto\zeta y$ is well defined because $(\zeta y)^r=(-1)(-1)=1$, it is diagonal (coefficient $k$ times $\zeta^k$) and hence an isometric isomorphism, and for $k+l=j+hr$ a wrapped term carries $\zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=\zeta^j(\zeta^r)^h(-1)^h=\zeta^j$, so untwisting recovers the cyclic coefficient with the correct sign.

quote.quote: Untwisting therefore recovers the cyclic coefficient with the correct sign.

children.claim: With $\iota$ identifying the last axis, of length $t_d=r$, with the coefficient lists of $T/r$ records in $\mathcal R_r$ and $(D_\pm f)_{\boldsymbol j,k}=\zeta^{\pm k}f_{\boldsymbol j,k}$, $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}=D_-\iota^{-1}\mathcal M_r(\iota D_+\cdot,\iota D_+\cdot)$ is a bilinear contraction equal to $(f*g)/T$, and $\iota$ moves no payload because both formats store the same words in the same order.

quote.quote: Hence $\iota$ and $\iota^{-1}$ change only the shape descriptor and require no payload movement when these component formats agree.

children.claim: The computed convolution $f'=Q_p(\widetilde\theta^+\cdot f)$, $g'=Q_p(\widetilde\theta^+\cdot g)$, $h'=\widetilde{\mathcal M}_r(\iota f',\iota g')$, $\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g)=Q_p(\widetilde\theta^-\cdot\iota^{-1}h')$ uses phase approximations of error below $2\,2^{-p}$ at total twist cost $O(Tp^{1+\delta})$.

quote.quote: Generating every factor anew therefore still gives total twist cost $O(Tp^{1+\delta})$.

children.claim: The computed chirp transform $\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(\widetilde a,Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)))$ has exact counterpart $QF_{\boldsymbol t}x$, and the source procedure $\widetilde{\mathscr F}$ (linewise $\widetilde{\mathcal A}$, then $\widetilde{\mathscr C}$, then linewise $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0$, then exact multiplication by $2^\gamma$) has exact counterpart $2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A=RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, with $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^+(z)=\overline{\widetilde{\mathscr F}(\overline z)}$ computing $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.
children.method: Compute the chirp phases modulo $2r$, conjugate the twisted complex convolution by them, and sandwich the resulting chirp transform between the linewise Gaussian maps.

motivation.text: The chirp and resampling identities say exactly which maps to compose, and every component is a contraction approximated on the disk grid, so the composite approximates $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ with additive errors.

children.claim: The chirp phase numerator at address $j$ is $-\sum_is_ij_i^2(r/t_i)\pmod{2r}$ with $r/t_i\in\{1,2\}$, computed with the established multiplier and exponential evaluation in $O(p^{1+\delta})$ per term, so building the chirp costs $O(Tdp^{1+\delta})$ and $\|\widetilde a-a\|_\infty<2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Thus chirp construction costs $O(Td p^{1+\delta})$ in total.

children.claim: Replacing every numerical subroutine by the exact map it approximates gives $\overline a\cdot\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(a,\overline a\cdot x)=QF_{\boldsymbol t}x$ and $2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A=RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ for $\widetilde{\mathscr F}$, while removing only sign-extension bits after the exact scaling keeps the scalar format.

quote.quote: Here an exact counterpart replaces every numerical subroutine by the exact map it approximates and omits truncations.

children.claim: The algorithm writes digit $a_j$ as the exact grid value $a_j2^{-b-2}$, applies $\Phi$ to obtain $u,v$ of norm below $1/4$, computes $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(u)$ and $\widetilde{\mathscr F}(v)$, multiplies them pointwise with one truncation to obtain $z$, computes $\widetilde{\mathscr F}^+(z)$ and scales by $S$ to obtain $\widetilde w$, scales by $2^{2b+4}S$ and rounds, applies $\Phi^{-1}$ and propagates radix-$2^b$ carries; the exact counterpart after the three transforms is $(u*v)/S^2$, so $w=(u*v)/S$ and $2^{2b+4}Sw$ is the original integer coefficient convolution.

quote.quote: The two occurrences of $S$ in this algorithm undo different normalizations.

children.claim: Every intermediate array stays in the unit disk without clipping and the final coefficient error is below $2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\,2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}<448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}\le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\frac12$, so rounding yields the exact integer coefficients and carry propagation yields the exact $2n$-bit product.
children.method: Propagate errors in units $h_p=2^{-p}$ through contractions (unchanged), bilinear contractions (added) and phase products (at most four units), keeping explicit norm margins $.7$, $.6$, $.5$, then undo the known scales exactly and round.

motivation.text: The true coefficients are integers, so an approximation within less than $1/2$ determines each by rounding; the work is to keep the accumulated error, magnified by the known scales $S$, $2^\gamma$ and $2^{2b+4}$, below that threshold, which $p=6b$ and $\gamma\le b/4$ ensure.

quote.quote: The true coefficients are real integers.

quote.quote: This proves the disk margin after the scale $M$, without clipping the output.

quote.quote: Each coefficient of $w$ is an average of $S$ products of coefficients of $u$ and $v$, so $\|w\|<1/16$.

children.claim: The integer coefficient array is $2^{2b+4}Sw$, and with $S\le T<2^b$ and $L<b$ the final absolute error is below $2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\,2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}<448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}\le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\frac12$, so the nearest integer is the correct coefficient, which lies in $[0,2^{3b})$ and fits a signed $(3b+1)$-bit word.

quote.quote: The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to that value the unique correct coefficient.

children.claim: The carries $k_0=0$, $d_j=(c_j+k_j)\bmod2^b$, $k_{j+1}=\lfloor(c_j+k_j)/2^b\rfloor$ satisfy $0\le k_j\le q(2^b-1)<2^{2b}$ and $\sum_{h<j}c_h2^{bh}=\sum_{h<j}d_h2^{bh}+k_j2^{bj}$, so one scan fixes the radix digits of the product, which is below $2^{2n}$ and is written in exactly $2n$ bits.

children.claim: With $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, every cost divided by $V$ is at most a power $p^{1-g_i}$ whose smallest margin is $2\kappa=2^{-181}$, or is $o(1)$, so the machine runs in $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$ for large $n$ and, with schoolbook multiplication below one fixed cutoff, in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for every $n$.

motivation.text: Since $p=\Theta(\log n)$, a normalized cost $p^{1-g}$ is a saving of $(\log n)^{-g}$; taking the smallest margin and keeping half of it leaves room for the fixed powers of $\log p$ hidden in the analysis.

quote.quote: This explicit slack will cover any remaining fixed power of $\log p$.
